title: Low-level Carbon Monoxide Line Polarization in Two Protoplanetary Disks: HD 142527 and IM Lup
question: Can CO, 13CO and C18O (J=2-1) line polarization from the Goldreich-Kylafis effect be detected, or tightly limited, in the protoplanetary disks HD 142527 and IM Lup, and how does 1.3 mm continuum polarization compare with 870 um?

data.sensitivity: CO(2-1) Stokes QUV noise 3.3 mJy per channel; continuum Stokes I rms 0.037 (HD 142527) and 0.022 (IM Lup) mJy/beam; QUV continuum 0.022 mJy/beam (Table 1)

what.value: 870 um ALMA polarization images of IM Lup (0.50'' x 0.40''), downloaded from the online version of the paper, used for the continuum comparison

evidence.quote: we downloaded the polarization images provided in the online version of (cite: Hull2018), which have a resolution of 0.50$''$ $\times$ 0.40$''$.

what.value: Disk models (stellar mass, inclination, position angle, characteristic radius) used as GoFish and morphological-model inputs

evidence.quote: We find estimates for most these parameters from disk models from (cite: PerezS2015) and (cite: Cleeves2016).
HD 142527 is a close binary system located 157 pc away (cite: Arun2019).
IM Lup is a K5 Class II T Tauri star located 158 pc away (cite: Alcala2017; Gaia2018).

what.value: Surface density profile form for the morphological model

evidence.quote: We assume a surface density profile that follows the form in (cite: Andrews2011)

what.value: Predicted GK line polarization of disks (PORTAL, CO(3-2)), compared with the observed limits

evidence.quote: So far, (cite: Lankhaar2020) has the only model that predicts line polarization for a disk.

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate on continuum and transfer solutions
recipe.method: Three phase-only self-calibration iterations on continuum Stokes I, with solutions applied to continuum Stokes QUV and line Stokes IQUV
tclean with Briggs weighting robust 0.5; continuum made from continuum baseband plus line-free channels; line continuum subtracted; primary-beam corrected
key_parameters: Robust = 0.5; pixel size 0.11''; continuum bandwidth 2.150 GHz

recipe.method: Compute polarized intensity, polarization fraction and position angle from Stokes IQU, with de-biasing following Hull et al. 2015
Gaussian fit of CO(2-1) QUV cube noise before primary-beam correction, moment 6 (rms) maps for spatial variation, and autocorrelation along the spectral axis

recipe.goal: Compare 1.3 mm and 870 um continuum polarization
recipe.method: Re-image archival 870 um HD 142527 data (calibrated by helpdesk) the same way, regrid and smooth to the common resolution; use published 870 um IM Lup images; compare polarized intensity, Pfrac ratio and angle difference
key_parameters: HD 142527 regridded to 0.06'' pixels; IM Lup to 0.1'' pixels

recipe.method: Solve numerically the line-ratio equation R = F1/F2 for tau, per channel and from integrated intensity maps, using isotopic ratios
assumptions: Flux-to-brightness-temperature conversion roughly identical for the lines (varies <1%), so flux ratio is used

recipe.goal: Model expected Q and U morphology
recipe.method: Build elliptical-polarization Q and U maps with Stokes I following a surface-density profile, smoothed to the beam and normalised to U_max, to choose stacking quadrants
key_parameters: HD 142527: PA = 160 deg, i = 28 deg, Rc = 200 au; IM Lup: PA = 144 deg, i = 48 deg, Rc = 100 au; gamma = 1
assumptions: Pfrac constant across the disk; surface density proportional to Stokes I

recipe.goal: Stack Stokes parameters along Keplerian rotation
recipe.method: Use GoFish to align spectra to deprojected Keplerian centroid velocities, stacking over the whole disk and over 90 deg quadrants (two starting angles, alternating rmin), for CO, 13CO, C18O
key_parameters: HD 142527: M* = 2.8 Msun, PA_red = 160 deg, i = 28 deg, d = 157 pc; IM Lup: M* = 1 Msun, PA_red = 144 deg, i = 48 deg, d = 158 pc; z0 = 0.1'' for both; IM Lup x-offset 0.8''
rmax where Stokes I drops to 90% of peak moment 0 value, rounded to 3'' (HD 142527) and 4'' (IM Lup); rmin alternates 0 and 0.17'' (HD 142527) or 0 and 0.5'' (IM Lup)
Other GoFish inputs left at defaults
assumptions: Keplerian rotation with inputs from published disk models

recipe.goal: Search for Q signal in optimised circular apertures
recipe.method: Inspect average spectra in circular apertures, then a custom script varying aperture size and position to maximise SNR_Q = |sum Q| / sigma over N consecutive channels, with channel covariance included
key_parameters: Aperture centred on a pixel with integer radii

recipe.goal: Monte Carlo test of aperture-search false-signal rate
recipe.method: Run the same SNR_Q maximisation at each 0.11'' pixel within 15'' of the map centre over a range of aperture radii and channel windows, to obtain the expected maximum SNR distribution
key_parameters: Aperture radii 1 to 27 pixels; 2 to 32 consecutive channels (~0.16 to 2.5 km/s)

recipe.goal: Derive pixel-by-pixel 3 sigma Pfrac upper limits
recipe.method: For each unmasked pixel find the channel sum maximising sum I over N channels and compute 3 sigma_PI sqrt(1.6N-0.6)/sum I, for several velocity intervals
key_parameters: Velocity intervals 0.5, 1, 1.5 km/s shown; sigma_PI = sigma_Q = sigma_U; pixels with moment 0 SNR < 10 masked

recipe.goal: Derive upper limits from stacked spectra and test robustness
recipe.method: Apply the same upper-limit equation to GoFish stacked spectra (whole disk and quadrants) using the noise of the Stokes V stacked spectrum; one thousand Monte Carlo runs perturbing mass, inclination and PA
key_parameters: Gaussian sigma of 15% for mass and 5 deg for inclination and PA

score_reason: ALMA data (project 2018.1.01172.S) are archival and results are numeric, but imaging details, channel selections and the custom aperture-search script are not given, and the detection significance depends on those choices.
rediscovery_reason: Data come from a single archived ALMA project, the main results are numeric (Pfrac, SNR_Q, upper limits) and the analysis algorithm (aperture SNR maximisation, GoFish stacking, upper-limit equation) is described in enough detail to redo approximately.
